paper_overrides.summary_setup: In-person computer-lab RCT at Middlebury College. Of 256 students assigned to AI-allowed or AI-forbidden conditions, 211 attended Session One and 205 attended both sessions. Students had a 35-minute learning phase on one of three unfamiliar topics (blockchain, carbon capture, CRISPR) and wrote an analytical essay. Only the AI-allowed group could use ChatGPT during Session One; both groups completed the knowledge tests and Session Two essay without AI. Incentives: $50 for completing both sessions plus lottery tickets ($100 each, 30 drawn) tied to test correctness and essay quality.
paper_overrides.summary_results: In the September 2026 version, immediate test scores rose by 0.292 SD (SE 0.121, p=.016). The one-week test effect was 0.202 SD (SE 0.116, p=.082). Overall essay-quality effects were positive but imprecise: 0.195 SD in Session One and 0.204 SD in Session Two. All five Session Two dimension estimates were positive; writing style had p=.058. Tests used 210 and 205 students; overall essay regressions used 210 and 198. The Session Two accuracy regression used 196.
